inputs.statement: V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generators x,y,h of sl₂(ℂ) act on V and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=λv.

output.statement: n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v; for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V, and y^(λ+1)v=0 (hence all higher lowering powers vanish). On this basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For all i∈I and natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

locals.declaration: Use t as the arbitrary induction index for the lowering-power identities.
Let i be arbitrary in I; each displayed coordinate calculation is valid for every such i.
Fix arbitrary complex coefficients c=(c_k) indexed by I for the linear-independence test.
Fix arbitrary j∈I for coefficient isolation.
Let r be an arbitrary natural number for the divided-power calculation.

argument.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

produces.statement: n=λ+1>0, |I|=n; for all integers t0≥0, h y^t0 v=(λ−2t0)y^t0 v, and for all integers t0≥1, x y^t0 v=t0(λ−t0+1)y^(t0−1)v.

argument.text: For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

produces.statement: For every i0∈I, e_i0≠0 and he_i0=(λ−2i0)e_i0.

argument.text: To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

produces.statement: (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

produces.statement: y^(λ+1)v=0; all higher lowering powers vanish; xe_0=0, xe_i0=(λ−i0+1)e_(i0−1) for 1≤i0≤λ, ye_i0=(i0+1)e_(i0+1) for i0<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i0=(λ−2i0)e_i0.

argument.text: Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.
